BiblicalUsage: He'ach is a cry, aha, the sound of someone gloating or exulting, and it is never a kind word in the Bible. In Ezekiel 25:3 Ammon says aha against the sanctuary, in Ezekiel 26:2 Tyre says aha against Jerusalem, and in Job 39:25 the horse says ha, ha, at the sound of the trumpet.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the cry gives the enemy away: aha is what you say when someone else falls, and the horse is the only one of the three with an excuse.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
